newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus to protest against pilgrimage cancellation.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus to protest against pilgrimage cancellation.

text.p: Cyprus will protest to the United Nations over the cancellation of a Greek Cypriot pilgrimage to the Turkish-held areas of the island for Greek Orthodox Easter, Cypriot officials said on Monday.

Turkish Cypriot officials said 118 people of the original group of 600 did go on the pilgrimage at the weekend, but Cypriot Foreign Minister Yiannakis Cassoulides branded it a lie by officials of the breakaway state to save face after they created obstacles for the rare visit.
"The Cypriot government will handle the matter accordingly both here and in New York," Cassoulides told reporters.
The 600 Greek Cypriots were scheduled to go to the monastery of Apostolos Andreas on the island's northeastern tip on Sunday.
But the pilgrimage was cancelled on Friday after Turkish Cypriot authorities insisted that some of the people on the list could not go, Greek Cypriot and United Nations officials said.

A number of people cited by the Turkish Cypriot authorities as having crossed into the Turkish-held north on Sunday were unrelated to the group initially planning to go to the monastery, Greek Cypriot officials said.

"This is a lie by the authorities of the pseudo-state which is meant to alleviate the very bad image they created of themselves with the obstacles they put up for the pigrimage to Apostolos Andreas," said Cassoulides, referring to the Turkish Cypriot administration which is recognised only by Ankara.
The pilgrimage would have been a first since the island's division in 1974 after a Turkish invasion sparked by a coup in Nicosia by the military then ruling in Greece.
The visit was to be in response to a visit by 435 Turkish Cypriot pilgrims to a mosque in the Greek Cypriot populated south this month to celebrate the Moslem Eid al-Adha feast.
The United Nations mission on the island plans several events over the next few months aimed at promoting goodwill between the Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities.
